trust_decision.summary: The sandboxed iframe page decides which DOM events (mousedown, focus, keydown) to forward to the parent as domEvent messages. At the pinned commit it forwards every event, synthetic ones included. The parent accepts any token-bearing domEvent and re-dispatches it into the session shortcut handlers.

landing_point.why: Only these listeners in the iframe page forward keyboard events to the parent, and a grep for domEvent leads straight to them.

fix_sites.entry_point: JS widget (Kino.JS) script running inside the JSView iframe dispatches synthetic mousedown/focus/keydown; new iframe/priv/static/iframe/v6.html adds isTrusted guards
fix_sites.module_kind: static iframe page in separate iframe/ mix app (served by LivebookWeb.IframeEndpoint / livebookusercontent.com)

fix_sites.entry_point: JSView hook getIframeUrl selects iframe page version (assets/js/hooks/js_view/iframe.js:50-52)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The fix's second file, assets/js/hooks/js_view/iframe.js:29,50-52, pins the iframe version and its SHA-256. This is coupling: the guarded page is only used if the pin is updated. It is not a separate route into the sink.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak. A solver could edit v5.html in place and call the checksum or versioning 'deployment' rather than the security fix. The legacy pages v1-v4 have the same unguarded listeners, but the checksum pin means the current client never loads them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A real user's keystrokes inside a focused widget must still reach notebook shortcuts (e.g. cmd+Enter evaluate, Escape) and Kino keyboard controls. The isTargetEditable routing to the hidden input must also keep working. A parent-side `if (!event.isTrusted) return` cannot tell real from fake input, because the parent always rebuilds the event synthetically, so it would block every proxied event.

O6_input_shapes: keydown (full KeyboardEvent props incl. ctrl/meta/shift/alt modifiers)
keydown with editable target (isTargetEditable routed to hidden input)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A keyup or input listener forwarded as domEvent next to keydown, with a matching replicateDomEvent branch.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: keyboard_control.js:34 already listens for keyup on the parent, so a maintainer adding keyup forwarding for Kino keyboard controls is plausible. WHERE-type only; it would fall to the same isTrusted fix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A parent-side message type (e.g. a shortcut/command message) that triggers session actions directly from a widget message without requiring user activation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: handleChildMessage already maps several child message types to session actions (selectSecret at js_view.js:392-397). The comment at js_view.js:362-368 treats shortcuts as low-risk.

O9_family: CWE-346 origin/provenance validation: untrusted synthetic UI events crossing a sandboxed-iframe postMessage bridge into parent keyboard shortcuts

O10_build.language: JavaScript (frontend) + Elixir (Phoenix server, iframe mix app)
O10_build.toolchain: Elixir ~> 1.18 / OTP, mix, Node/npm for assets
O10_build.project_tests: None for this area: no JS tests for js_view or iframe pages (assets/test only covers lib/ and session cursor_history, collab_client). Behavioural checks need a real browser engine to produce isTrusted=true events.

j.j_sites_touched: iframe/priv/static/iframe/v6.html (new, copy of v5.html with isTrusted guards); assets/js/hooks/js_view/iframe.js
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an isTrusted check in the parent session.js/js_view.js handlers, which blocks all proxied events, or edit v5.html in place without updating IFRAME_SHA256/version, which breaks iframe loading or never reaches the cached hosted copy.

out_of_scope_notes: The same fix release lists other CVEs (notebook import path traversal, shell escaping, Teams ZTA, Teams login CSRF); none touch this sink.
Programmatic element.focus() inside the iframe can produce a trusted focus event; the impact is limited to focusing the cell and was not pursued.
unverified: j_defence_ineffective=1 refers to the token check (assets/js/hooks/js_view.js:369), which authenticates the iframe but cannot tell the widget's synthetic events from real ones. It is not a broken check in the usual sense.
Whether a hidden behavioural test can be built without a real browser (jsdom cannot produce trusted events) is unknown; a headless browser is likely required.

Legacy iframe pages v1-v4 (iframe/priv/static/iframe/v1.html:139, v4.html:182) are still served by IframeEndpoint but rejected by the current client's checksum pin (assets/js/hooks/js_view/iframe.js:62); older Livebook clients were not examined.
